messages:
Alex: heads-up — we're seeing sustained admission throttles on the committed pool in ap-northeast-1 starting ~09:12 UTC. queue depth spiked, several tenants getting 429/admit_rejected. Not seeing node OOMs.
Rina: on it. any recent deploys or new commitments?
Alex: new enterprise commit went live at 09:05 and started a sustained batch workload. autoscaler didn't spin added nodes quickly.
OpsBot: [ALERT] reserved-pool-apne1 admission_rate_limit triggered (threshold=0.85). 60s avg queue_depth=420.
Samir: dumping metrics now — pushing p95 latency + admit_rejected counts.
Samir: ```
# metric snapshot
pool=ap-northeast-1-commit
queue_depth: 420
admit_rejected: 312 (last 10m)
active_nodes: 18
target_nodes: 20
autoscaler_last_scale: 2024-03-?? 08:58 UTC
```
Leah: autoscaler minReplica was 0 on this pool after the config sync last week? that would make cold scale slower.
Miguel: correct — we patched a pool template and accidentally removed min=2. rolling patch hit apne1 template.
Rina: ok that explains slow spinup. short term: can we enable emergency override to admit critical tenants + throttle best-effort?
Alex: proposing: 1) emergency admit override for tenants with tier in [enterprise, sla-critical]; 2) rate-limit lower tiers to 20 rps; 3) trigger manual scale + open temp burst nodes (2x GPUs) from capacity pool.
Leah: manual scale command ready: `infractl pool scale --name apne1-commit --add-nodes 2` but provisioning ETA ~14-18m.
Samir: implemented traffic steering change to fallback hosted models for non-critical tenants (rollback route applied). monitoring show drop in new queue inflow ~30%.
OpsBot: [ACTION] Route change applied by Samir at 09:30 UTC.
Rina: started admit override script to bump enterprise weight. will watch SLOs.
Alex: running smoke on enterprise tenant A — previously saw 429 on create-infer. retesting.
Alex: enterprise A ok now (no 429s), p50 latency back to normal for their sessions.
Miguel: scaled pool manually at 09:44 UTC. infra reports new nodes provisioning.
OpsBot: [INFO] node-provision apne1-commit node-203 provisioning_started
Samir: note: our rate-limiter ladder currently uses absolute token buckets per-tenant. we hit a corner where many medium tenants' accumulated bursts saturated admission. considering moving to weighted fairshare.
Leah: long-term fix items: 1) revert accidental template change (minReplica) + add unit test in infra pipeline; 2) add per-zone cold-start buffer (keep min spare nodes); 3) implement weighted fairshare admission for committed pools.
Rina: cost tradeoff call: adding 2 hot nodes costs ~ $46/hr. keeping 2 spare nodes permanently ~ $46/hr baseline. recommend spare buffer on high-demand AZs only.
Alex: agreed. short-term: keep the 2 nodes until midnight UTC, then autoscale back down. create a billing justification.
Miguel: filed infra PR to restore minReplica=2 and pipeline test -> #PR-3647.
Samir: opened an incident follow-up doc and postmortem checklist. I'll add admission metrics + replay.
Alex: next steps owners: Miguel -> revert template PR, Samir -> postmortem + metrics dashboard, Rina -> customer comms for affected enterprise tenants, Leah -> implement per-zone buffer design doc.
Leah: we should also add an alert for template changes that remove minReplica. risky.
Rina: sending one-line status to oncall channel and paging product ops for comms.
OpsBot: [RESOLVED] admission_rate_limit cleared at 10:06 UTC. queue_depth trending down to 40.
Alex: closing Slack coordination. we'll sync in the postmortem meeting at 14:00 UTC. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Miguel: adding cost estimate + retention window to the follow-up.
Samir: will attach scrubbed tenant IDs to the PM doc for evals.
Rina: filing customer notes now.
Alex: good job. incident label: pool-saturation-apne1, severity: S2.
